title: Multi-source research diamond
intent: Decompose one question into independent per-source jobs, run them in parallel, and merge them at exactly one fan-in barrier that verifies citations, deduplicates claims across sources, and reports contradictions instead of resolving them.
nonGoals: It does not fetch anything. Every source result in this bundle comes from the deterministic mock adapter and a committed fixture.
It does not enforce a budget. See policy.budget.enforcement.
It does not enforce a permission or an isolation boundary. See policy.permissions.enforcement.
It does not judge which side of a contradiction is right; it reports both positions with their citations.
It does not retain partial results when a source fails permanently. See limitations.partialSourceFailureRetention.

graphs.note: Both documents are byte-equivalent after canonicalization, and both language runners assert that against the constructor output before running anything.

constructors.parity: Both constructors produce the same canonical document; the runners assert equality against the committed graph in each language.

fixtures.note: The expected events and the expected report live in files. The runners and the package tests compare against them; they never restate them inline.

adapters.note: No real provider adapter exists in this repository. See docs/patterns/research-diamond.md#real-provider-setup for what would have to be supplied.

tests.crossLanguage: Both runners compare against the same fixtures/expected-events.json and fixtures/expected-run.json; agreement between the lanes is what the shared files enforce.
tests.note: There is no automated packed-install test for this bundle, and no CI job runs the two example runners. They are run by hand.

budget.note: These numbers are documentation, not a control. No runtime component in this repository reads or enforces a token, money or time budget; the budget contract is D10-* and is contract-only. The only numbers that actually bind a run are the Graph IR policies (maxConcurrency, maxFanOut, maxTotalAttempts) and each node's retry.maxAttempts, which the scheduler does enforce.

modelRouting.declared: One model-shaped adapter per source, selected by source key.
modelRouting.note: Routing here is executor wiring in the example, not a runtime policy object.

permissions.note: There is no isolation provider, so nothing enforces any of this. The reason the runs perform no network access is that the code contains no network call and the mock adapter cannot make one — not that a sandbox refused it. The shell adapter in this repository refuses execution for exactly this reason.

approval.note: This pattern has no human approval step. No approval provider exists.

redaction.declared: Durable payload protection is configured and mandatory; every authoritative value reaches the journal as a protected reference under the default capture policy.
redaction.enforcedBy: durable payload protection; a durable run without it fails closed with PAYLOAD_PROTECTION_REQUIRED before the first event and the first executor call
redaction.note: Both runners assert the fail-closed path.

retention.declared: In-memory journal and payload store for the examples; nothing is written to disk.

retry.where: resume.mjs / resume.py, scenario A — GE_ADAPTER_RATE_LIMITED injected on attempt 1 of source-web

crashAndResume.where: resume.mjs / resume.py, scenario B — the journal commits and then loses the process; the resumed run never re-invokes the committed source

replay.where: resume.mjs / resume.py — resuming an already terminal run returns the recorded result with zero new events and zero executor calls

failClosedWithoutProtection.where: resume.mjs / resume.py — PAYLOAD_PROTECTION_REQUIRED, zero executor calls

timeout.reason: A deterministic timeout demonstration would need a controllable clock in the run path; this bundle reads no clock at all, by design.

cancellation.reason: Cancellation during synthesis is a listed Pattern 01 negative case. It is not demonstrated here.

fork.reason: Replay/fork of a durable run is not exercised by this bundle.

partialSourceFailureRetention.reason: The merge node is a static all-success barrier. If one source fails permanently the barrier is never satisfied and no partial report is produced. Retaining partial sources needs quorum or settled barrier behaviour, which is capability-gated and not implemented.

diagrams.traceVisualization: Both runners emit an event-order trace showing the three source lanes overlapping and the barrier waiting. The scale is the journal sequence number, not wall-clock time.

limitations.noRealProvider: Nothing in this bundle has ever contacted a provider. There is no provider client in this repository.
limitations.noObservabilityBackend: There is no metrics or tracing backend. The observability queries in the launch guide are journal projections, not queries against a running system.
limitations.noSupportBundleTool: There is no support-bundle command. The launch guide documents what to collect by hand.
limitations.noIndependentReview: This bundle has not been independently reviewed.
limitations.notInCi: No CI job runs the two example runners.
